impl:b9-compound.summary:
B9 is done in one commit, c72e56b, on branch ccr-ccc6d89a-5cxd7e (not pushed). A `direction` inside a subgraph or state composite is now honoured.

**What changed.** New module /home/user/flowmaid/src/compound.rs. A subgraph becomes a "block" when its own direction differs from the one around it, at least two of its members link to each other, and no member links outside it. `split()` cuts the graph into its outermost blocks plus the rest. Each block is laid out on its own, in its own direction; blocks nested inside blocks are handled the same way, recursively. In the rest, each block is a rectangle placeholder the size of its frame, so edges to the subgraph end on the frame like on any node, with normal ports, labels and outline snapping. The parts are then joined back. The scene contract is unchanged: nodes stay in graph order, graph edges come first and sub-edges after in order, frames are outermost-first at their real depth.

**Interactive path.** `route()`, `route_sized()` and `route_partial()` split the same way: each block is routed in its own direction, then the rest is routed around the block's frame as it currently stands. Dragging inside a block grows its frame and redraws the edges to the frame; a drag outside leaves the block alone. A new crate-internal `route_partial_with` carries the frame sizes. Picking matches what is drawn, because the joined scene is exactly what the painter draws.

**Bars and quality harness.** `fit_bars` now lays a fork/join bar across its block's own flow. The quality harness measures `wiggles`, `frame_side` and `lat_wiggles` for an edge inside a block along that block's direction. Nothing changes for graphs without blocks.

**Mermaid's rule, checked with mmrender.js (mermaid 12.2).** A direction holds only while no member links to a node outside the subgraph; edges to the subgraph itself are fine. A member linking to its own subgraph, or an edge into a subgraph nested inside it, counts as linking out. A subgraph with no direction keeps the parent's. One correction to the brief: mermaid applies this rule to state diagrams too — a composite whose inner state is linked from outside is drawn as a column. So both diagram types use the same rule, and it is documented in README.md.

**Result.** examples/state.mmd: the `Validating` composite is a 413×92 row and the canvas 535×873, down from a 126×368 column on a 403×1133 canvas (mermaid: 459×109 in 649×886). Mermaid's documentation example (TB, RL and BT blocks nested in an LR chart) also comes out as mermaid draws it.

**Effect elsewhere.** None of the 79 corpus, fixture and example inputs changes except state.mmd. Over the 1351 flowchart/state sources in the scratchpad bulk set that have a `direction` line, 277 change:
- crossings 1110 → 932
- edges through frames 78 → 54
- defects 376 → 316 static and 396 → 366 routed
- edges running on top of each other 76 → 106, mostly in hub fans to blocks
- canvas grows a median 22%, because a column becomes a row

**Speed.** `perf.sh b9-compound` stays within budget; the worst-frame drag on the 75-node bench is 20.67 ms against 20.22 ms before. A fuzz run over the 277 changed graphs (`route`, zero sizes, 3 drags per node through `route_partial`) gave no panics and only finite geometry.

**One gate changed.** In `note_links_match_between_scene_and_route` the elbow floor drops from 63 to 61. Its first source's `Outer` composite (`direction TB` in an LR diagram, nothing linking out) is now laid out top-down, and two of its note links run straight. Scene and route still match for every link.

**Still to do at the next release:** docs/img/compare/state.png in the README still shows the 0.35.0 column; it should be regenerated.

problems: (non-blocking, contract) A fork/join bar that branches to a block composite now changes size when you drag a state inside the block. This breaks the released promise 'dragging never resizes a bar' (CHANGELOG ~l.891, fit_bars doc at src/scene.rs:7246-7248). Repro with my harness bardrag.rs: x7-fork-to-block.mmd, drag `d` +250 px, and bar f goes from 321x8 (scene) to 446x8 in both route_partial and route. x8 (LR state with a TB block): drag `e` +200 px and f goes 8x328 -> 8x428. Cause: the rest part's fit_bars sizes the bar from the proxy, i.e. the block's frame as it stands now (compound.rs:858-873 -> scene.rs route_partial_with raw_sizes override). fit_bars(whole graph) also no longer predicts the drawn length (150 vs 321). Since parts refit with max(), a route_sized host that passes back the sizes it drew keeps the grown bar after dragging back. Either document this or keep the scene's bar length while dragging.

(non-blocking, docs/parity) In state diagrams, mermaid lays out a composite that has no `direction` of its own top-down, whatever the diagram's direction. r2-state-nodir-lr.mmd (`direction LR`, an isolated composite P with a->b->c) draws P as a column in mermaid; flowmaid inherits LR and draws a row, as it did before this package. CHANGELOG and README say 'The rule is mermaid's, for flowcharts and state diagrams alike' with no direction meaning inherited. Keeping inheritance is defensible (do not copy mermaid quirks), but the difference should be stated.

(non-blocking, layout) A block is always ordered after sibling nodes that were created before its first member, whatever the declaration order. In x9-order.mmd (`S --> s` then `S --> Q`), x7 and x8 (`f --> P` before `f --> Q`), the block sits right of or below the sibling. Mermaid, and the pre-package layout, put it first. Pre also ignored declaration order (it always put the subgraph first), so this is not strictly a source-order regression, but output flips relative to pre and mermaid. Cause: the proxy slot sits at the first member's node index (compound.rs:364-377), and block sub-edges become rest edges appended after all graph edges (compound.rs:433-474).

(non-blocking, quality) A block's proxy is one big node in its layer, so it widens that layer for sibling subgraphs. Bulk f114.mmd (LR, only g3 TB is a block): the 'aliqua aliqua' frame and its n1->n2 edge come out about 3x wider than pre. f259 is similar, and there a thick hub edge hugs the TB block's left and bottom borders at about 7 px. This accounts for the implementer's bulk overlap_pairs 76 -> 106 and the 87 bulk files with more defects (92 have fewer). The implementer did report these numbers honestly.

(nit) compound.rs:1101-1102 `let (labels, sizes) = crate::layout::node_texts(&g); let _ = labels;` should be `let (_, sizes) = …`. docs/img/compare/state.png in the README still shows the old column (the implementer flagged it for the next release).

Everything the spec asked for is in place. The state composite LR is one row; a flowchart LR subgraph with no outside links is a row; one with outside links keeps the parent direction; mermaid's rule is verified with mmrender.js and documented; route(), route_sized() and route_partial() lay blocks out as scene() does; hit-testing matches the drawing; drag budget is kept.

Pre (40a2923) measured 13.59, 12.59 and, in 3 later alternating runs, 12.30 / 13.20 / 13.14 ms; now measured 11.72 / 17.83 / 17.78. A dedicated alternating timer gave best-of minimums of about 12.0 ms (now) vs 11.8 ms (pre). Counted as noise.
